case_table.case_body_summary: Constructs two std::string objects (sizes 32 and 512) from packet body at +0x10 and +0x34, then calls FUN_004d8560 with a 2-byte selector at packet+0x30, the local_978 (32-byte) string and the local_920 (512-byte) string. Both std::strings are destructed via FUN_00446f50 in reverse order. FUN_004d8560 itself: returns char; calls FUN_004b4ed0(1), FUN_00c99e80(param_4, 1, ret, 1), and on success FUN_00445c70 -> FUN_004c3dd0 -> FUN_004ce760(param_2, param_3, param_4) gated by zone+0x660. Pattern shape: 'execute named command with arg string'.
case_table.notes: Two strings: 32-byte (likely command name) + 512-byte (likely arg/parameter blob), keyed by a u16 selector at packet+0x30. The FUN_004ce760 inner call uses param_2=incoming sender, param_3=cmd name std::string, param_4=arg std::string. Could be the 'admin/debug command' or 'chat command parser' s2c entry point.

case_table.case_body_summary: Toggles zone+0x54b flag. If was 0: sets to 1, calls FUN_004de800(zone+0x1780c) to grow vector at zone+0x1804/+0x1808/+0x180c capacity; walks intrusive doubly-linked list rooted at zone+0x17804 (uses FUN_00944d70 iterator, FUN_0071b730 deref); for each entry whose +3 field is not in {-0x3FFFFFDC, -0x3FFFFFF9, -0x3FFFFFFB} runs FUN_004d87f0 (returns true if entry+0x80 non-zero AND FUN_00574aa0 returns non-zero); if not, calls FUN_004de190(entry_id) and if zero skips, else calls FUN_00813050(entry_id). Then FUN_004b7340 (audio/world manager reset), FUN_00578230. Builds a second list via FUN_006cfbb0/FUN_0071cb30, iterates calling FUN_004d9910(id) and invoking actor->vftable[0](1) (scalar-deleting-dtor). Calls FUN_004d9980(0xc0000000) to clear active target, FUN_0057a3c0(zone+0x174f4, zone+0x174f8, zone+0x554, zone). Final loop iterates actor list calling FUN_00575390(actor+0x10+0x80) (Pattern A on each actor's +0x80 substruct). Else branch (flag was 1): clears to 0 and calls FUN_004d8080(1) which conditionally invokes FUN_004dfaa0/FUN_004dfad0 against zone+0x174ec when zone+0x17838 (active player) is null.
case_table.primary_handler: 0x004daf00 (mirror cleanup helper - FUN_004daf00 implements an almost identical actor-list-walk-and-destruct, shared logic) OR inline case body (no single primary)

0x004d9980 (active target reset = the c0000000 sentinel - shared with cases 0xE and 0x11)
case_table.notes: By far the largest low-switch case body (~150 lines of decomp). Functional shape is 'zone tear-down to char-select / zone-change': clears active target, runs filtered actor list walks twice (with a 3-value 'preserve' filter at entry+3), invokes per-actor dtors, drains the audio/timer subsystem, rebinds zone state. The flag at zone+0x54b acts as a re-entry guard - second toggle becomes a no-op-ish client-side init path. The very similar FUN_004daf00 helper (case 0xE primary) duplicates much of this logic but with different filter sources and additional sound/transition prep; case 4 and case 0xE are siblings of the same teardown family.

case_table.case_body_summary: Fallthrough with cases 0xD and 0x10: `if (*(int **)(zone+0x4e0) != 0) (**(code **)(**(int **)(zone+0x4e0) + 0x24))(iVar8);` - reads the object pointer at zone+0x4e0, invokes vftable slot 9 (offset 0x24) on it, passing the packet pointer.
case_table.notes: **Multi-case fallthrough group**: opcodes 0x5, 0xD, 0x10 share this single body. Structurally identical to BCS-Y-0527 (the actor-vftable9 fallthrough for 24 opcodes 0xF/0xCC..0xE5) EXCEPT: the dispatch target is the object at zone+0x4e0 - NOT the actor map. zone+0x4e0 is a distinct sub-object pointer with its own vftable. The 'actual handler' is whatever class owns *(zone+0x4e0), and its vftable[9]. This is a Pattern A receiver dispatch through a different cluster than the actor map. Investigation of (*(zone+0x4e0))->vftable layout is a follow-up question for whoever picks up the receiver cluster work.

case_table.case_body_summary: Single call: `FUN_0081eb90(zone+0x950)` (zone+0x950 was bound to local_9f8 at function entry). FUN_0081eb90 reads vector range [zone+0x954, zone+0x958], asserts ordering via FUN_009d22b4, then calls FUN_00440940(local_8, vec_struct, begin, vec_struct, end) - a vector-range visitor.
case_table.notes: Pure vector flush/dispatch on zone+0x950. The vector at zone+0x950 is the SAME vector that cases 8/9/A/B append into. So case 6 is the 'flush all queued vector entries' command - it iterates the entire range and invokes FUN_00440940 (an std::for_each-shaped helper) on the contents. zone+0x950 is the shared 'pending operation queue' for cases 6/8/9/A/B.

case_table.notes: Out of scope here (the actor-cluster-dispatch-model pass caught this). Included for completeness of the case table.

case_table.case_body_summary: Conditional 1-entry-style loop guarded by `*(char*)(packet+0x10) != 0`: vector_struct = zone+0x17810; entry_ptr=(undefined4*)(packet+0x14); does `do { local_a0c=(undefined8*)*entry_ptr; local_a08 = byte_at(packet+0x34+i); FUN_0081f090(zone+0x950, &(value,flag_byte_pair)); i++; entry_ptr++; } while (i < (uint)*(packet+0x10))`. So entry count is bounded by the byte at packet+0x10 (max 255 but variable). Values come from packet+0x14..; flags from packet+0x34..; both vectors are independent strides.
case_table.notes: Variable-length pair-array append. Pair = (u32 value, u8 flag). Appends each pair to the shared zone+0x950 queue. FUN_0081f090 either does an in-place pair push when capacity allows, else FUN_0081ee20 (reallocating push).

case_table.notes: Fixed count = 16. Flag array at packet+0x50 (= +0x10 + 16*4 = +0x50, consistent with 16 u32 values followed by 16 flags). Packet payload size for this case = 0x60 bytes.

case_table.case_body_summary: Fixed 32-entry loop, values at packet+0x10+i*4 and flags at packet+0x90+i. Identical inner logic to cases 8/9/B.
case_table.notes: Fixed count = 32. Flag array at packet+0x90 (= 0x10 + 32*4 = 0x90). Packet payload = 0xB0 bytes.

case_table.case_body_summary: Fixed 64-entry loop, values at packet+0x10+i*4 and flags at packet+0x110+i. Identical inner logic to cases 8/9/A.
case_table.notes: Fixed count = 64. Flag array at packet+0x110 (= 0x10 + 64*4 = 0x110). Packet payload = 0x150 bytes. Cases 8/9/A/B form a sized-array family: 1..255 / 16 / 32 / 64 entries respectively, all feeding the same zone+0x950 vector via FUN_0081f090.

case_table.case_body_summary: Single call: `FUN_004bbb30(*(undefined2*)(packet+0x10), *(undefined1*)(packet+0x12))` - passes a 16-bit ID and 8-bit selector. FUN_004bbb30 is a sound/UI fade-state machine: gated by `InterlockedExchangeAdd(&DAT_0132f3d0, 0) == 1` (only proceeds if a global busy flag is set), then dispatches on the second arg (which it calls param_2) to 11 actions: -10000 / 1 / 2..14, mostly calling FUN_004b7650 (audio fade), FUN_00b908f0 (animation/sound trigger), FUN_004b56c0 / FUN_004b5710 / FUN_004b5740 (sound state mutators) at param_1 + 0x7fe0000.
case_table.notes: Scalar pair = (u16 audio_id, u8 action_code). The 'param_1 + 0x7fe0000' offsetting strongly suggests param_1 is a small zone-ID treated as an index into a memory-mapped audio bank base. Pattern shape: bgm/sound cue trigger with state transitions. Could be 'PlayBgm' / 'StopBgm' / fade variants.

case_table.case_body_summary: Three-step shutdown: `FUN_004d9980(0xc0000000)` clears the active target/player ref, `FUN_004daf00()` runs the large zone-cleanup helper (1708 bytes - iterates and destructs filtered actor list, then re-runs init, calls FUN_004b7340 audio reset, FUN_0057a3c0 zone-state-rebind), then conditional `if (*(int *)(zone+0x4bc) != 0) FUN_00565aa0(0xb)` - emits a state-change-to-0xB notification (FUN_00565aa0 updates obj+0x98, then invokes (*(obj+0xa0))->vftable[1] which returns flags; if bit 0x2 is set runs FUN_004d6f40(0) (or for state 0x15 the FUN_004d73b0/FUN_005670b0 alt path)).
case_table.notes: Case 0x11 has the EXACT same shape: `FUN_004d9980(0xc0000000); FUN_004daf00(); if (zone+0x4bc != 0) FUN_00565aa0(0xc);` - the only difference is the state code passed to FUN_00565aa0 (0xb vs 0xc). Case 0xE = state 0xb (likely 'logout' / 'returning'); case 0x11 = state 0xc (likely 'zone-change' / 'transferring'). FUN_004daf00 is the canonical 'zone-leave / actor-cleanup' helper, called by case 0xE, case 0x11, and FUN_004db5b0.

shared_case_body_descriptions: Cases 0x5 + 0xD + 0x10 share one Pattern A body: dispatch to vftable[9] on (*(zone+0x4e0))
Cases 0x8 + 0x9 + 0xA + 0xB share the same pair-append inner: FUN_0081f090 on zone+0x950 (sized 1..255 / 16 / 32 / 64)

Three-step zone-leave cleanup: clear active target via FUN_004d9980(0xC0000000), run full zone teardown via FUN_004daf00 (large 1708-byte helper), then if zone+0x4bc != 0 emit a state-change-to-0xB notification via FUN_00565aa0 (which propagates to the observer at obj+0xa0 vftable[1]). Pair with case 0x11 (state 0xC) - this is the 'enter logout state' opcode; 0x11 is 'enter zone-change state'.

key_findings: Case grouping identified: cases 5/0xD/0x10 share ONE Pattern A fallthrough body (dispatch to vftable[9] on *(zone+0x4e0)). This is a distinct receiver cluster from the actor-map vftable[9] cluster (BCS-Y-0527) - same architectural pattern, different target object. Three opcodes catalogued under a single BCS-Y entry (BCS-Y-0537).

Case grouping identified: cases 8/9/A/B form a sized-array family that all append (u32 value, u8 flag) pairs to the shared queue at zone+0x950 via FUN_0081f090. Cases 8/9/A/B counts are 1..255 / 16 / 32 / 64. Case 6 is the corresponding 'flush' opcode that drains zone+0x950 via FUN_0081eb90 - so opcodes 6 + 8 + 9 + A + B form a producer/consumer set against the same in-memory queue.

Case 0xE and case 0x11 are sibling shutdown opcodes - identical bodies except for the state code passed to FUN_00565aa0 (0xB vs 0xC). Both delegate the heavy work to FUN_004daf00, which is the canonical zone-leave/actor-teardown helper. Case 4 is structurally a third sibling but with a re-entrancy toggle and slightly different teardown filters.

FUN_004daf00 (case 0xE primary) and the case 4 body inline very similar actor-list-walk-and-destruct loops, both with the same 3-value preserve filter at entry+3 ({-0x3FFFFFDC, -0x3FFFFFF9, -0x3FFFFFFB}). The two filter sentinels are u32-encoded class IDs in the 0xC0000000 family (see BCS-Y-0533 ZoneActorClassId_Validate) - they are the IDs of three actor classes that survive zone teardown (likely the local player, the camera, and one other persistent actor).

Case 3 is the 'execute named command' s2c entry point: 32-byte cmd name string + 512-byte arg string + u16 selector. Routes through FUN_004d8560 -> FUN_004ce760 gated by zone+0x660. The inner pipeline is the same shape as a Lua command bridge - this opcode is plausibly the 'server-pushed lua script execute' or 'admin command' path. Pattern matches the existing ExecuteDebugCommand receiver cluster in the symbols.json notes.

Case 0xC drives a global audio cue state machine (FUN_004bbb30) protected by an atomic busy flag (DAT_0132f3d0 set via InterlockedExchangeAdd). The 'param_1 + 0x7fe0000' base-offset pattern indicates an mmap'd audio bank addressed by ID. 11 action codes route to fade / start / stop / state-set variants. Likely the s2c BGM trigger.

Of 10 cases, 0 cataloged, 10 uncataloged. 1 Pattern A (5/D/10 shared body), 9 Pattern C. No Pattern D sub-dispatchers found in this slice (sub-dispatchers were the pattern-d-subdispatcher pass finding).

11 new proposed BCS-Y entries: 10 function_case entries for the dispatcher case bodies (one is shared by 3 opcodes - 5/D/10), and 1 function entry for the FUN_0081f090 pair-append helper. Last existing ID was BCS-Y-0534; first proposed is BCS-Y-0535. NO BCS-Y entries written to symbols.json - manifest is draft-only per workspace rules.

No new emissions found. None of the 10 cases call FUN_004E0240 (the c2s emitter that case 7 uses) or any other identified outbound sender. The cases are pure receivers / state-mutators / cleanup helpers.
open_questions: What class lives at zone+0x4e0? Its vftable[9] is the actual handler for opcodes 0x5, 0xD, 0x10. zone+0x4e0 vs the actor map (zone+0x17804/+0x17808 area) is a distinct sub-system; resolving it requires finding writes to zone+0x4e0 elsewhere in the binary and reading the vftable layout. Follow-up candidate.

Cases 8/9/A/B emit (u32 value, u8 flag) pairs to zone+0x950. What does case 6 ultimately DO with those pairs? FUN_00440940 (the visitor inside FUN_0081eb90) is uncataloged. The semantic interpretation of the u32 value and u8 flag depends on FUN_00440940. Worth a follow-up decomp.

The case 4 'preserve filter' values {-0x3FFFFFDC, -0x3FFFFFF9, -0x3FFFFFFB} are class IDs (= 0xC0000024 / 0xC0000007 / 0xC0000005 in u32). Per BCS-Y-0533, these are 'engine-managed' actor classes. Mapping these three IDs to actor class names (via the registry at FUN_00d35af0) would name the persistent zone actors.

Case 0xC's FUN_004bbb30 uses param_1+0x7fe0000 as an mmap base. Need to confirm param_1 (u16 audio_id from packet+0x10) is bounded and what bank lives at base 0x7fe0000 relative to the audio context. This is musical/sfx state and worth its own phase.

Case 3's std::string sizes (32 + 512) and FUN_004ce760 inner call look identical to a Lua command bridge invocation. Worth correlating with the Lua engine attribution phases (32/41) to see if FUN_004ce760 is in the Lua bind cluster.

Case 4 sets a zone+0x54b flag; case 0xE/0x11 do NOT toggle this flag - they always run the full cleanup. Why does case 4 have a re-entry guard but cases 0xE/0x11 do not? Suggests case 4 is the 'pause' opcode and 0xE/0x11 are the irreversible logout/zone-change opcodes.

FUN_004d9980's 0xC0000000 sentinel: BCS-Y-0533 confirms this is the 'invalid class id that intentionally fails validation' value. So `FUN_004d9980(0xC0000000)` is the canonical 'clear active target' call. Worth promoting FUN_004d9980 itself to BCS-Y in a follow-up since it's used by cases 4, 0xE, 0x11 and likely many other clear-target sites.
